switch), started 2026-10-03 23:48 and written 2026-10-04. It is an implementer-side checker, not the item's author. It
re-checks the item after its second fix round `build/M0-d-01-fix2` (LANDED 2026-10-03 23:47) on round r1's F-5 and F-6.
Protocol: `M0.md` §3 steps 1 – 5. The failed line (2) and the item's whole test set were re-run, every other checklist
line was gone through again, and a fresh set of mutants was aimed at what rounds 0 and r1 had not tried. Rounds r1 and
0 are kept below, unchanged.

## Verdict: FAIL — F-5 and F-6 closed; five new failing lines (F-7 – F-11), each one or two test assertions; the code is correct

F-5 and F-6 are closed. Fix round 2 changed no source file and removed no assertion, and its two new tests kill round
r1's four survivors (K48, K70, K71, K50). Every gate and every here-bar is green.

This round ran 29 source mutants and one type-level mutant in scratch mirrors. Nine survived. One is equivalent (R18)
and one changes a refusal that no clause or row states (R3, note N13). The other seven fall into five failing lines.
Each changes a behaviour that the item's own choices row C-0143 (or §6.1's helper contract) states, and the item's tests
are that row's named holder. So each fails line 2 by the standard rounds 0 and r1 applied: a test that cannot fail on a
path the item's contract relies on. In every case the item's code is right — a probe passes on it — and only the pin
is missing:

* **F-7.** The seed key's four salts are not pinned (C-0143 (1): SHA-256's first four round constants). Changing them
  together re-keys every stream of every document and passes all 95 tests.
* **F-8.** `keyText`'s "each non-zero component" rule is pinned for the epoch only (C-0143 (4)). Rendering `/r=0`,
  `/a=0` or `/s=0` passes.
* **F-9.** `KeyCensus` can be made to call a collision a reuse, and no test sees it (C-0143 (6)). With its length check
  removed, a source that extends an earlier source of the same hash counts as a reuse. The API takes sources of any
  length, and no test adds two of different lengths.
* **F-10.** `Rng.stream`'s stage parameter can be widened back to a plain `number` with no compile or test failure.
  C-0143 (3) chose the `StageId` brand, and the `@ts-expect-error` lines hold it on `streamKey` only.
* **F-11.** `weighted`'s half-open interval at an exact running-sum boundary is not pinned. A mutant that takes the
  lower index there, still skipping zero weights, passes. At `float01() = 0.5`, `weighted([1, 1])` returns 0 instead of
  1: a bias of one grid point in 2²⁴, the class of round 0's F-3 and r1's F-6.

The fix is about ten added test lines in four test files, and no source change. Note N17 suggests how the fix round
can close the series instead of leaving the next check to find more.

## Round r1's failing lines — closed

* **F-5 (the width halves).** `test/rng/mixer.test.ts:253 – 281` ("refuses every field outside its width on each side —
  negative, fractional, too wide, NaN — and accepts both ends") refuses, for each of reroll, attempt, epoch and salt,
  the negative, fractional, too wide, NaN and infinite values. It accepts 0 and the largest lawful value, and it does
  the same for the stage and the concern. Each refusal is matched to its own message (`<field> must be`), so a refusal
  by another field cannot satisfy it. K48, K70 and K71 are each red on exactly this test (`exit 1; × refuses every
  field outside its width on each side …`). **Closed, CONFIRMED.**
* **F-6 (`int`'s rejection limit).** `test/rng/stream.test.ts:126 – 153` builds keys with `inverseOdd` whose first
  output is the limit, or one below it, for spans 3 · 2³⁰, 3 and 10. It asserts the redraw at the limit, the keep below
  it and the draw counts, and it pins r1's key `[1, 0x33800000, 2, 3]` → 11 520. K50 is red (`exit 1; × draws again on
  an output exactly at the rejection limit …`). **Closed, CONFIRMED.**

Against round r1's scratch mirror, `diff -rq` over `src/rng/`, `src/registry/`, `test/vectors/xoshiro/` and
`vendor/xoshiro/` is empty. In `test/rng/`, only three files differ:

* `mixer.test.ts` gains 30 lines and loses none.
* `stream.test.ts` gains 33 lines; its three header-comment lines were rewritten.
* `invert.ts`'s header comment changed (one line out, two in).

No assertion was removed.

## The failing lines

### F-7 — the seed key's salts (C-0143 (1)) are not pinned to their values

`src/rng/mixer.ts:45` declares `SEED_SALTS`, and `:47 – 50` hold the same four values as `SALT0` … `SALT3`, which
`seedKey` and `laneKey` use. The seed-key tests (`test/rng/mixer.test.ts:28 – 57`) compare each lane with
`fmix32(SEED_SALTS[i] ^ seed)`, so they read the constant itself; they also check that the four are distinct. No test
states their values.

Mutant R1 changes `SALT0` and `SEED_SALTS[0]` together (`0x428a2f98` → `0x428a2f99`): `exit 0; 95 passed (95)`. Under
R1 every seed key, entity key and stream key differs, while C-0143 (1) still names the SHA-256 constants. The analogous
published constant, the zero-state nudge, is pinned by value (`test/rng/stream.test.ts:46`). (Round 0's K7 changed one
lane's salt alone, which the lane test does catch.)

Probe P1, on the item's code (the built bundle), computed the constants independently as the fractional parts of the
cube roots of 2, 3, 5 and 7: `SEED_SALTS 428a2f98 71374491 b5c0fbcf e9b5dba5 | cube-root constants 428a2f98 71374491
b5c0fbcf e9b5dba5 | equal true`. It also gave `seedKey(0)` = `b30705af baaedc8b b0675f61 0889e26d`.

**Required change:** in `mixer.test.ts`, assert that `SEED_SALTS` equals `[0x428a2f98, 0x71374491, 0xb5c0fbcf,
0xe9b5dba5]`, as `stream.test.ts:46` pins the nudge. A known answer of `seedKey(0)` (above) is a cheap end-to-end pin
beside it. Show R1 red.

### F-8 — `keyText`'s "each non-zero component" rule (C-0143 (4)) is pinned for the epoch only

`src/rng/text.ts:79 – 82` appends `/r=`, `/a=`, `/e=` and `/s=` only for a component that is given and is not 0. The
`keyText` test (`test/rng/rng.test.ts:207 – 215`) passes `epoch: 0` once, so the epoch's rule is held. It never passes
`reroll`, `attempt` or `salt` as 0. Mutants R2, R2a and R2b each drop the `!== 0` test for one of them, and each gives
`exit 0; 95 passed (95)`. Under them the textual form reads, for example, `S11/siteplan@plot:…/r=0/a=0/s=0`.

Probe P2, on the item's code: `keyText` with all four components given as 0 gives `S11/siteplan@plot:7kq2m9x4c1b0a`.

The form is for reports only, so the harm is small. But the rule is the row's, and `rng.test.ts` is its named holder.

**Required change:** assert P2's output, with all four components given explicitly as 0. Show R2, R2a and R2b red.

### F-9 — the census tells a collision from a reuse only for sources of one length (C-0143 (6))

`src/rng/census.ts:115 – 121` (`sameSource`) compares the two sources' lengths first. C-0143 (6) says the census
"tells a reuse (the same source again) from a collision (two sources, one hash)", and `add` takes "`source` (any number
of u32 words)" (`:81`). The collision test (`test/rng/rng.test.ts:169 – 178`) uses sources of one length only.

Mutant R4 removes the length check: `exit 0; 95 passed (95)`. Under R4 a hash recorded from `[9, 9]` and then from
`[9, 9, 7]` counts as a reuse. That hides a collision from the distinctness bar M0-d-09 runs on this harness (§6.1,
"the test guards the encoder").

Probe P4, run in the mirror: on the item's code it gives `new, collision`. Under R4 it gives `new, reused`
(`AssertionError: expected 'reused' to be 'collision'`).

**Required change:** assert that a longer source after a shorter one with the same prefix is a collision. The reverse
order is a cheap companion assertion, though R4 does not reach it. Show R4 red.

### F-10 — `Rng.stream`'s `StageId` brand (C-0143 (3)) is held by no compile-time line

C-0143 (3) says "`stream`'s stage parameter is the kernel's `StageId` brand (§14 writes `number`; C-0134 (9))". It names
"`corepack pnpm build` (its `@ts-expect-error` lines)" among its tests. `test/rng/no-string.test.ts:165 – 174` holds
the brand on `streamKey` (a stage given by name, a plain number) and the concern on `Rng.stream`. No line passes a
plain-number stage to `Rng.stream`.

Type-level mutant T3 types `Rng.stream`'s stage as `number` (`src/rng/rng.ts:19, 51`, with one cast to call
`packInto`). With T3, `tsc -b` on the kernel's two projects exits 0 and the rng tests give `95 passed (95)`. Under T3
the runtime still refuses an unregistered stage, so what is lost is the compile-time check the row chose.

Probe P10 ran in a second scratch mirror. Adding `// @ts-expect-error` before `rng.stream(EK, 11, CONCERNS['cut.stop'],
O)` compiles on the item's code (exit 0). Under T3 it fails: `no-string.test.ts(173,5): error TS2578: Unused
'@ts-expect-error' directive.`

**Required change:** add that line. Show T3 red.

### F-11 — `weighted`'s boundary convention is not pinned (§6.1 `weighted(table)`; C-0143 (2))

`src/rng/stream.ts:147 – 152` returns the first index whose running sum exceeds `u = float01() · total`. That is the
half-open interval from the sum before the index to the sum after it. It is the same convention as `float01`'s own
[0, 1) and `bool`'s `float01() < p` (C-0143 (2); round 0's F-3), and it makes the draw exactly proportional for dyadic
weights, as the doc comment's "chance proportional to its weight" asks. The tests cannot see a change at the boundary:

* the twin test (`stream.test.ts:278 – 286`) uses total 10, whose running sums 1, 3 and 6 no `u` can equal exactly;
* the frequency test (`:288 – 301`) works within 3 s.e.;
* the zero-uniform test (`:303 – 308`) has zero weights only at the boundary.

Mutant R23 (`u < acc` → `u <= acc && weights[i] > 0`: the closed interval, with zero weights still skipped) gives
`exit 0; 95 passed (95)`.

Probe P11 builds a key whose first `float01()` is exactly 0.5, with word 1 from `inverseOdd`, as `stream.test.ts:129 –
132` does. `weighted([1, 1])` gives `1` on the item's code and `0` under R23 (`AssertionError: expected +0 to be 1`).
Under R23, index 0 gets 2²³ + 1 of the 2²⁴ grid points and index 1 gets 2²³ − 1: the one-point bias round 0's F-3
named for `bool`.

**Required change:** add P11's assertion to `stream.test.ts`. Show R23 red.

## The rule this round applied (so the fix round can apply it too)

A surviving mutant is a failing line when two things hold:

* the behaviour it changes is stated by a design clause or by the item's own choices row (C-0143, C-0147), on an input
  the API admits;
* the item's tests are the row's named holder.

It is a note when no clause or row states the behaviour (round r1's N9; R3 here), or when it is equivalent (round 0's
K36; R18 here). Under this rule F-7 – F-11 fail, and R3 and R18 do not.

  precondition, which is N9's class. Probe P3 on the item's code: `weighted -1e-9: refused`. The fix round may add
  `-1e-9` to the refused list at no cost.

  not tried. The fix round can end that. In its scratch copy, it can run one mutant per constant and per comparison or

## The failing lines

### F-5 — the refusal test does not hold the full width of attempt, reroll and epoch (the encoder guard)

C-0143 (3) says the mixer refuses "any field outside its width". §6.1 gives the widths: reroll u16, attempt u8,
epoch u32. Round 0's F-2 made one point about salt: a component's width check is what keeps two distinct tuples from
packing to one word, so the refusal test must hold it. `packInto` (`src/rng/mixer.ts:150 – 153`) checks every
component in full. The refusal test (`test/rng/mixer.test.ts:224 – 251`) holds only some halves of those checks:

* attempt: only the cap (`cut.stop` 1, `cut.t` 3, `naming` 9). There is no negative or non-integer attempt.
* reroll: only `65536`.
* epoch: only `2 ** 32` and `1.5`.

Three mutants survive the item's whole test set (`vitest run --project kernel packages/kernel/test/rng` in the
mirror):

| mutant | change | result | probe on the mutant (the item's code refuses each) |
|---|---|---|---|
| K48 | `!(isU16(attempt) && attempt <= cap)` → `!(attempt <= cap)` | `SURVIVED (exit 0; 93 passed (93))` | `P48 attempt 1.5 -> key 3559061526,1545904119,2924736525,4042549318 (EQUAL to attempt 1)` |
| K70 | `!isU16(reroll)` → `!(reroll <= 0xffff)` | `SURVIVED (exit 0; 93 passed (93))` | `P70 reroll -1: ACCEPTED, key EQUAL to {"reroll":65535,…}`; `P70 reroll 1.5: ACCEPTED, key EQUAL to {"reroll":1,…}` |
| K71 | `!isU32(epoch)` → `!(Number.isInteger(epoch) && epoch < 4294967296)` | `SURVIVED (exit 0; 93 passed (93))` | `P71 epoch -1: ACCEPTED, key EQUAL to {…,"epoch":4294967295,…}` |

On the item's code the same probes print `refused` for each value and pass (`orig exit 0`). So the code is right.
Only the test cannot fail.

**Required change:** in the refusal test, assert that each of these is refused:

* attempt −1 and 1.5 (for example on `cut.t`);
* reroll −1 and 1.5;
* epoch −1.

Show K48, K70 and K71 red.

### F-6 — `int`'s rejection boundary (C-0143 (2): "an output ≥ 2³² − 2³² mod span is drawn again") is not pinned

`src/rng/stream.ts:95` redraws while `u >= limit`. The test that names the boundary is "draws one output when it is
below the rejection limit, and redraws above it (unbiased)" (`test/rng/stream.test.ts:109 – 123`). It compares 2 000
draws against a twin's `>=` loop, and it meets an output exactly at the limit with chance about 2 000 / 2³²
(≈ 5 × 10⁻⁷). Mutant K50 (`u >= limit` → `u > limit`) gives `SURVIVED (exit 0; 93 passed (93))`. Under K50 an output
equal to the limit is kept, giving `lo + 0`, so the value 0 gets one extra output in 2³²: the bias the rejection exists
to remove.

This is round 0's F-3 class, a boundary a constructed key reaches. A probe in the mirror built such a key,
`[1, 0x33800000, 2, 3]`. Word 1 is `inverse(5) · rotr(0xc0000000 · inverse(9), 7)`, so the first output is exactly the
limit for span 3 · 2³⁰. The probe printed `P50 first output 3221225472 = limit 3221225472; correct int = 11520`.

* On the item's code, `int(0, 3 · 2³⁰ − 1)` returns 11 520, and the probe passes.
* Under K50 it returns 0: `AssertionError: expected +0 to be 11520`.

**Required change:** add that assertion to `stream.test.ts`. Build the key from `inverseOdd` in `test/rng/invert.ts`,
as the probe does, and assert the redraw against the twin. Show K50 red.

## The failing lines

### F-1 — `Rng.stream`'s bucket-collision path is untested: "a second request returns the same stream" cannot fail there

`src/rng/rng.ts` keeps a derivation's streams in a `Map` keyed by 30 bits of key word 0 (line 56). A bucket that
holds more than one stream becomes an array, which is searched on lookup (line 62) and extended on insert (lines 67 –
68). No test reaches that path. Two mutants survive the item's whole test set (`vitest run --project kernel
packages/kernel/test/rng` in the mirror):

* K1 removes the array search (`for (const s of found) if (sameKey(s, key)) return s;` becomes `;`). Result:
  `SURVIVED (exit 0; 90 passed (90))`.
* K2 drops the push (`else found.push(made);` becomes `else {}`). Result: `SURVIVED (exit 0; 90 passed (90))`.

The path is live in real use. A scratch probe in the mirror built 10⁵ entity keys under one seed and requested the
`S11` / `siteplan` stream of each in one derivation. It printed `PROBE buckets shared: 4; first
[[228,88072],[4596,39496],[31053,57796]]`. On the item's code, every second request returned the same `Stream`
(`Tests 1 passed`). Under K1 the same probe failed (`AssertionError: expected false to be true`): a second request
created a fresh stream restarted from its key. That breaks §6.1's "a second request in the same derivation returns the
same stream". K3-probe (the bucket narrowed to 2 bits, which forces the array path everywhere) stayed green
(`90 passed`), so the array code is correct today. Only its test is missing.

**Required change:** add a test to `test/rng/rng.test.ts` that drives `Rng.stream` through shared buckets. It must
cover at least one bucket of two streams and one of three or more, so that the push path runs too. It then requests
every stream again, asserts `toBe` identity and asserts `rng.streams`. A natural pair is found by search, as in the
probe above. A bucket of three is easiest to build by inverting the finaliser round: `mixer.test.ts` already has
`unfinalise`. Choose three stream keys that share word 0's low 30 bits, and take entity key = `unfinalise(k)` ⊕
packed. The fix round shows K1 and K2 red.

### F-2 — the refusal test does not hold salt's u16 width (the encoder guard)

`packInto` refuses a salt outside u16 (`src/rng/mixer.ts:150`, `if (!isU16(salt)) refuse(R_SALT, salt);`). The
refusal test asserts only `salt: -1` (`test/rng/mixer.test.ts:270`), which a u32 check also refuses. Mutant K34
(`isU16(salt)` becomes `isU32(salt)`) gives `SURVIVED (exit 0; 90 passed (90))`. Under K34 a salt of 2¹⁶ or more ORs
into the reroll half of word 1. Then (reroll r + 1, salt s) and (reroll r, salt s + 2¹⁶) pack to one word, which
silently voids the distinctness guarantee §6.1's encoder guard rests on. Reroll's bound is tested
(`reroll: 65536`, line 269), and K35 is red.

**Required change:** assert the refusal of `salt: 0x10000` (and, for example, `2 ** 32`) in the refusal test, and show
K34 red.

### F-3 — `bool(p)`'s boundary (C-0143 (2): `float01() < p`; the docstring's "p ≤ 0 never") is not pinned

`src/rng/stream.ts:102` returns `this.float01() < p`. The test "never at p ≤ 0" (`test/rng/stream.test.ts:137 –
140`) draws 1 000 random uniforms, none of them exactly 0, and the twin test compares at p = 0.5. Mutant K16 (`<`
becomes `<=`) gives `SURVIVED (exit 0; 90 passed (90))`. Under K16, `bool(0)` is true once in about 2²⁴ draws. The
author killed the same boundary in `weighted` (their M19) with a key whose first uniform is exactly 0.

**Required change:** with the same key (`[1, 0, 0, 0]`, whose first `float01()` is 0), assert `bool(0) === false`. Also
assert, for example, that `bool(2 ** -24)` is true on that draw. Show K16 red.

### F-4 — the builds' entity-key cache ("cached beside the lineage hash") has no owner, test or staging record

The item's `builds` (M0-work.json) says "the entity key (seed key ⊕ lineage hash ⊕ arena key, cached beside the lineage
hash)", and §6.1 says "computed once when the entity is minted and cached in the arena beside the lineage hash". The
item builds the pure `entityKey()` but no cache. Its only statement of where the cache lives is a code comment,
`src/rng/mixer.ts:10`: "(§6.1; the cache is the arena's)". C-0143 does not mention the cache. No other item's `builds`
names it either: M0-a-02's arena holds the interned handles but no lineage hashes or entity keys. M0-d-05a's
`sections` carry "§6.1 (the entity key from the lineage hash)", and its `mint` is where "computed once when the entity
is minted" would happen. M0-x-02's `StageContext.stream` takes a `Handle` and must find the key. A clause the item
names, with no test and only a code comment pointing at an owner that does not build it, fails line 2.

**Required change:** append a choices row under the C-0104 id rule that names the cache's home and the test that will
hold it there. The reading the twin supports is M0-d-05a's `mint`, beside the lineage hash it mints. Alternatively, the
row may stage the cache with its milestone. Make the `mixer.ts` comment say the same. (PLAUSIBLE: which item is the
better home is the fix round's reading; that a home must be recorded is CONFIRMED.)
